stories.title: Australia says information on 34 missing citizens in Nepal is ‘very limited’
stories.summary: At least 34 Australian citizens are missing in Nepal after deadly floods caused by a mud and rock collapse into a Himalayan river. Many missing Australians were part of pilgrimage and tour groups, including 15 Indian-Australians on a religious tour to Mount Kailash. Rescue efforts face challenges due to limited access and information; a tourism chief estimated a 1% chance of survival in the flood zone. Australia Foreign Minister Penny Wong said on Aug 27 at least 34 of its citizens on pilgrimages and tours in Nepal were missing following deadly floods, but information there was “very limited”. More than 1,000 people including at least 600 foreigners are missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet, authorities said on Aug 27, after a wall of mud and rock collapsed into a Himalayan river, sending catastrophic floods through towns and valleys. Wong said at least 34 Australians were among the hundreds missing. “We understand these Australians are part of separate pilgrimage and tour groups,” she told a news conference on Aug 27. “At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster... we are urgently seeking to confirm the welfare and whereabouts of Australians.” Himalayan Glacier, a tourism agency operating in the area, confirmed 15 of the missing Australians were on a religious tour to Mount Kailash it was organising. The group also included people from India, the US, Canada and Singapore. “They were on a pilgrimage.

stories.title: Cook Islands Party wins fifth term as official results come in
stories.summary: Aug 26 - The Cook Islands' Mark Brown looks set to stay as prime minister of the island nation after official election results on Wednesday showed his Cook Island Party won 13 of parliament's 24 seats to clinch a fifth term. The results showed four seats won by the Cook Islands United Party, with the remaining seven going to a mix of independents and minor groupings. The main opposition in the last parliament, the Democratic Party, failed to win a seat. The vote comes at a sensitive time for the Cook Islands' ties with New Zealand, with which it is in free association.

stories.title: Nvidia quarterly revenue more than doubles to $96.2 bln
stories.summary: The corporation expects revenue of around $108 bln in the next quarter
article_sentences: NEW YORK, August 27.
US technology giant Nvidia more than doubled its revenue in the Q2 of its current fiscal year compared with the same period a year earlier.
Nvidia’s current fiscal year began on January 26, 2026, and will end on January 31, 2027.
Nvidia reported revenue for the second quarter ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 bln, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago, the company said in its report.
The corporation posted revenue of $46.7 bln in the Q2 of the previous fiscal year.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) in connection with the release of the financial results.
The corporation expects revenue of around $108 bln in the next quarter, according to the report.
